productRequirement.summary: Build a new Northstar API Keys management experience that does not already exist in the repository. Workspace admins need to browse and search keys, create a key with an access scope, inspect key metadata, and revoke a key with confirmation.
userGoals: Browse API keys with name/prefix identity, access scope, status, and a record-specific details action.
Search keys by name or key prefix.
Create a key with a required display name and one access scope: Read only or Read and write.
Inspect key details including name, prefix, scope, status, created by, and created date.
Revoke an active key only after an explicit consequential confirmation.
dataFixtures: Production deploy — prefix nsk_prod_7H2 — Read and write — Active — created by Amal Hassan.
Analytics reader — prefix nsk_analytics_4F9 — Read only — Active — created by Sara Ahmed.
Legacy integration — prefix nsk_legacy_2K1 — Read only — Revoked — created by Amal Hassan.
API key prefixes are intrinsically LTR even when the surrounding UI is Arabic.
This evaluation does not require revealing, copying, or storing an actual secret token value.
requiredStates: Create-key modal with validation and successful creation.
Key detail open with selected-row association.
presentationModes: Wide Application Shell and compact/narrow directory presentation.
For any contextual-detail behavior that approved guidance marks unresolved on narrow screens, report the unresolved decision instead of inventing a new model.

executionRules: Read only the shared agent-context allowlist from the test-pack manifest; do not read any denied source.
Do not inspect git history, pull-request diffs, other branches, tags, or earlier implementations to recover an answer.
Do not use external search or external code examples to locate or imitate an implementation.
Use only public governed package APIs authorized by the supplied contracts and guidance.
Do not add or modify design-system components, contracts, patterns, tokens, or canonical guidance.
Write implementation files only inside the task writeRoot.
Use governed tokens when available and explain every remaining local raw dimension or local CSS decision in AUTHORING-REPORT.md.
When supplied authorities do not resolve a decision, record it as unresolved in AUTHORING-REPORT.md instead of guessing.
Do not ask a human to correct the implementation during the run.

checks.statement: Select governed components/patterns appropriate to the new API-key domain instead of inventing custom controls or table/detail primitives.
Do not invent public component props, variants, states, slots, or events for the unfamiliar domain.
Use local CSS only where approved composition/product ownership permits it and document every such decision.
Do not introduce arbitrary raw colors or duplicate governed layout/spacing values merely because this is a new screen.
Generalize the approved Directory, Modal List → Detail, and Create Flow guidance into the new API-key domain.
Preserve accessible names for search, repeated row actions, create/revoke Dialogs, detail focus ownership, and consequential confirmation.
Use logical RTL/LTR layout and preserve API key prefixes as intrinsic LTR data.
Generalize the governed directory responsive rules and explicitly escalate unresolved narrow contextual detail.
The unfamiliar API-key screen should still look and behave like a coherent Northstar product surface built from the governed DS.

expectedEscalations: Narrow-screen contextual API-key detail presentation remains unresolved and should be reported rather than invented.
contaminationSignals: new public DS APIs created only to solve this evaluation
